    11  /-!
    12  # Hitting times
    13  
    14  Given a stochastic process, the hitting time provides the first time the process "hits" some
    15  subset of the state space. The hitting time is a stopping time in the case that the time index is
    16  discrete and the process is strongly adapted (this is true in a far more general setting however
    17  we have only proved it for the discrete case so far).
    18  
    19  ## Main definition
    20  
    21  * `MeasureTheory.hittingBtwn u s n m`: the first time a stochastic process `u` enters a set `s`
    22    after time `n` and before time `m`
    23  * `MeasureTheory.hittingAfter u s n`: the first time a stochastic process `u` enters a set `s`
    24    after time `n`
    25  
    26  ## Main results
    27  
    28  * `MeasureTheory.Adapted.isStoppingTime_hittingBtwn`: a discrete hitting time of an adapted process
    29    is a stopping time
    30  * `MeasureTheory.Adapted.isStoppingTime_hittingAfter`: a discrete hitting time of a adapted process
    31    is a stopping time
    32  
    33  -/
    34  
    35  @[expose] public section
    36

    39

    41  
    42  namespace MeasureTheory
    43  
    44  variable {Ω β ι : Type*} {m : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    45  
    46  section Basic
    47  
    48  variable [Preorder ι] [InfSet ι] {u : ι → Ω → β}
    49

    51  /-- Hitting time: given a stochastic process `u` and a set `s`, `hittingBtwn u s n m` is
    52  the first time `u` is in `s` after time `n` and before time `m` (if `u` does not hit `s`
    53  after time `n` and before `m` then the hitting time is simply `m`).
    54  
    55  The hitting time is a stopping time if the process is strongly adapted and discrete. -/
